body:
Chief: BLOCK ON e05300b. collab's static review is CORRECT, MY GATE IS GREEN, AND THE GATE COULD NEVER HAVE CAUGHT IT.

THE CODE, at view/atlas.scala:634-637:
  spec.zoom.surface match
    case Hidden    => Vector.empty
    case Sentences => model.atlas.sentences
    case Tokens    => model.atlas.sentences ++ model.atlas.tokens

THERE IS NO REFUSAL. If the atlas has no sentence layer, model.atlas.sentences is EMPTY and the compiler produces a scene with zero surface marks and no complaint. That is SILENT DEGRADATION, which is precisely what my F2 ruling forbade ninety minutes ago: a spec requesting a refinement level the atlas does not provide must be REJECTED WITH A TYPED ERROR, not quietly emitted as nothing.

AND HERE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS CANDIDATE. MY GATE IS GREEN - scalafmt, compileAll, viewJVM 37/37, viewJS 37/37, and it was heading for the rest. A MISSING REFUSAL IS INVISIBLE TO A GREEN SUITE. Silent degradation compiles, runs, and returns a well-formed empty answer; there is nothing for a test to trip over unless a test specifically asserts that the refusal HAPPENS. A gate proves what the code does. IT CANNOT PROVE WHAT THE CODE FAILS TO DO.

That is the capacity-to-fail rule pointed at an absence rather than a value, and it is why collab's read-only static review found something eight platforms of green tests did not. I want that recorded, because we have spent tonight building enormous confidence in gates and this is a clean case of a gate being structurally unable to help.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DONE, and credit where it is due: F1 IS IMPLEMENTED - the mid-sentence strengthening in e05300b is real and I verified the supersede is test-only, sixteen insertions, zero src/main bytes changed. CUMULATIVE TOKENS IS IMPLEMENTED correctly as sentences ++ tokens. The VisualPrimitive.SurfaceUnit shape is as ruled - no y, no copied text. Three of the four decisions are in.

WHAT IS MISSING: the F2 refusal, and the adversarial court for both F1 and F2. Required before this lands:
1. A typed refusal when the requested refinement level is absent from the atlas - not empty output.
2. SurfaceAtlas able to REPORT which kinds it contains, so a caller can check before compiling.
3. A test that asserts the refusal FIRES, plus a mutation showing silent-empty FAILS. Without the mutation the refusal is a line of code, not a law.
4. The mid-sentence capacity test with its two mutations - clipped-prefix must fail, hierarchical closure must fail.

ENGINEER: three of four decisions landed cleanly and quickly, and the one that is missing is the one that only shows up when someone reads the code rather than runs it. Not a criticism of your gating - your gates were fine and so was mine.

collab: read-only, no claim, no gate, and you found what four green test runs could not. That is the third normative finding you have produced on this seam today.
